newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Esso Singapore maintains 15-pct cut in crude run.
newsitem.headline: Esso Singapore maintains 15-pct cut in crude run.

text.p: SINGAPORE, Sept 26 (Reuter) Esso Singapore Pte Ltd, an affiliate of U.S. oil gaint Exxon Corp, is still maintaining a 15-percent cut in crude run at its 230,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery, a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.
Esso reduced its operating rates in early July due to poor refinery margins. It is the only refinery in Singapore that has yet to restore operations back to maximum capacity.
An Esso official earlier told Reuters, the company preferred to wait until margins are firmly in the black before resuming full operations.
Refining margins slipped back to the red sometime in early September when crude prices soared following the U.S. missile attacks on Iraq, accomponied with a rise in product prices.
"The margins are fluctuating due to middle distillate prices which are also moving back and forth," one refiner said.
Primary refining margins for Arab Light crude have moved over the past few days from $1.00 per barrel to a 20 cents per barrel, the refiner said.
In early September, Mobil Oil Singapore and Shell Singapore, which had also reduced runs, resumed full production in early September, spokesmen for the two refiners said earlier.
